# 3 Axial Skyrmions
- The reflection alters the sign of only one pion field, meaning the relative phase used here differs by an added π compared with refs. [3, 12, 7], where an antiSkyrmion is formed by reversing the signs of all three pion fields.
- This convention is adopted because it allows a more natural comparison with the analogous monopole configuration.
- As indicated in (3.10), the profile function vanishes at a distance s/2 from the centre of the Skyrmion or antiSkyrmion, allowing the pair to be joined continuously while setting the fields to the vacuum outside their cores.
- Besides the initial conditions from the simple ansatz (3.7), more refined initial data were also constructed using the rational map ansatz [11] with an axially symmetric charge n map.
